findings.claim: Rebuilding compact defaults or Board/Flow would duplicate delivered source capability.
findings.change: Retain existing output/observer modules; extend their execution, context and freshness semantics only.
findings.rationale: The real gap is integration and decision correctness, not a missing board or compact switch.

findings.claim: Requiring GATE-810/OUTCOME-810 before independent later implementation would serialize work without consumed artifacts.
findings.change: Use the shared interface contract as the hard dependency and integration-requires for actual composition; order cumulative acceptance at gates.
findings.rationale: Implementation, verification and delivery are different constraints. Shared core/CLI edits still have one integration owner.

findings.claim: A fourth final gate or per-task full-suite rerun would duplicate cumulative proof.
findings.change: Final intent reuses GATE-830; later gates refresh inherited proof only where current inputs or new composition require it. Available commands are not a mandatory checklist.
findings.rationale: All requirements are covered at the final cumulative boundary; source/permission freshness checks remain mandatory.

findings.claim: This planning session cannot establish native host interfaces, actual savings, independent-review provenance or human comprehension.
findings.change: Validate availability early, preregister measurements and keep missing required evidence blocking final acceptance; no fixture or stdout proxy substitutes.
findings.rationale: These are explicit qualification tasks, not unearned plan facts. Future authority requirements cannot be granted by this candidate.

findings.claim: Hashes, registry entries and inventory alone do not prove execution, permission or deletion eligibility.
findings.change: Separate instrumentation provenance from semantic truth and host permission; test forged/stale/unknown-owner cases and independently review consequential boundaries.
findings.rationale: Local receipts must disclose their trust limit; cleanup and retries require exact ownership/reference/process checks.

findings.claim: Current seven coarse asset locators do not yet cover all proposed new modules and planning paths.
findings.change: Keep assurance as incomplete hypotheses; assess and narrow assets through canonical interfaces in CONTRACT-801 before source work and real parallel scheduling.
findings.rationale: Do not label a new module mapped or an inspection performed based solely on this generated draft; existing baseline/history remains preserved.

findings.claim: Adding system behavior to the mixed 6,031-line core without an ownership/extraction contract would amplify maintenance and context cost; mechanically splitting files would not resolve authority boundaries.
findings.change: Add three responsibility-bound extraction tasks, extend existing CLI/Observer owners, preserve facades/serialized contracts and keep the original three cumulative gates. Limit initial schema edits to observed duplicate domains; qualify offline consumers.
findings.rationale: These tasks protect separate publication, behavior and serialized-compatibility boundaries. Node growth is corrective decomposition, not a claim of runtime complexity or token savings.

findings.claim: Zero command counters cannot establish absent skill/API usage, equivalence or safe removability; aggregate size/version differences cannot establish current-source model savings.
findings.change: Include all-command/all-skill scenario dispositions; retain recovery capability and simplify default routing first. Matched current-source evaluations and actual host accounting establish benefits; proposed deletion without equivalence remains deferred.
findings.rationale: Rare recovery has asymmetric loss prevention; direct APIs and agent-only skills are unmeasured. Historical high-output modes are targets for qualification, not current-source bug verdicts.

findings.claim: Extraction integration needs a real consumed store/use-case interface, but a global schema write scope or whole-refactor acceptance dependency would unnecessarily serialize independent work.
findings.change: Use TASK-841 → TASK-842 → TASK-813 as the consumed interface chain, integration-requires for schema composition, and six explicit schema edits rather than every schema. Recompute changed waves and hypothetical scheduling; preserve conservative shared-helper/schema conflicts until supported mapping is narrowed.
findings.rationale: Disjoint feature modules keep the common contract as their start dependency. Safe concurrency is not inferred from levels or an old batch ID.

summary: Refine the user-approved full-system scope with three responsibility-bound architecture/schema tasks: 16 work nodes, 3 cumulative gates and 11 intent requirements. Preserve the original requirement/constraint/non-goal contract while adding user-requested maintainability and scenario-based surface justification. Reuse the actual CLI audit and exact source inventory; no canonical transition, implementation, deletion, claim or qualification pass is implied.
limitations: Single-coordinator semantic planning review; not an independently dispatched reviewer or executed product qualification.
Plan/schema/graph validation can establish structural legality, not task correctness or achievable token savings.
Source remains dirty and pending history code binding; no commit, installation or publication is implied.
Assurance draft contains planned hypotheses only; new paths and narrow ownership must be assessed before application. The draft is not automatically imported by new-intent.
Representative real host and consented engineer evaluation need qualified interfaces, available observations and applicable authority. Required unknowns remain blockers, not passed.
Usage is daily local aggregation across projects and recorded 4.0/4.1 versions; no project/sequence/skill or direct-API attribution, no causal waste estimate and no current 4.2 savings verdict.
Schema comparisons confirm selected equal/unequal definitions, not all 31 domains' equivalence; CONTRACT-801/TASK-843 complete the ownership and offline-consumer matrix.
Hypothetical scheduling keeps TASK-841/TASK-843 serial under coarse draft asset inspection assumptions and actual shared helper-schema writes; no current canonical batch or permission is created.
